newsitem.title: UK: NWE low sulphur fuel oil slides again with crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE low sulphur fuel oil slides again with crude.

text.p: NWE low sulphur fuel oil prices fell sharply again on Wednesday as sagging crude oil futures took the ground away from an already long market, traders said.
Dealers said they saw 200,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel on offer for the next 15-18 days, and no signs of fresh buying interest from Italy.

Latest Italian industry data showed Italy's power generation sector bought 1.70 million tonnes of high and low sulphur fuel oil in December, a fall of 17.7 percent from December 1995. Purchasing of fuel oil by the power sector in all of 1996 was 22.35 million tonnes, 4.3 percent down from 1995.

One dealer said had offered a low sulphur cargo at swaps levels in the morning but declined to say at what levels he was offering in the afternoon. February low sulphur swaps were assessed at $109/$110 fob NWE in late business, after a small rally in crude futures.
High sulphur fuel oil was slightly softer. An ARA player was heard having sold a cargo to a U.K. utility at $110 cif NWE, but this deal could not be confirmed.
High sulphur barges traded as low as $106.50 fob ARA in the morning, but rose later to talk at $108/$109.
